producthunt.author: danshipit
producthunt.body:
RankSpot: Pay-as-you-go SEO and AI Search execution layer for agents RankSpot is the SEO and AI Search execution layer for agents. Connect the MCP to Claude or ChatGPT in 2 minutes and your agent does the work: it writes articles from what already ranks on Google in 100+ languages, publishes them, and pitches ranking sites from your mailbox for backlinks. Run every client or business from one chat. No subscription: $3 an article, $0.004 a prompt check, reading your data free. Start with $1 of credit and a free article.

Hey Product Hunt 👋

Dan here, co-founder of RankSpot.

Last time we launched, RankSpot only generated content on autopilot. Since then we've onboarded 1,000+ customers, and their feedback shaped our improved product. So we set out to build something no other SEO tool could do, and focused on these things:

1️⃣ Execution → Most SEO tools stop at the data

Congrats on the launch! Does it support Shopify?

Running a small web agency, the "manage multiple clients from one chat" part is what caught my eye. Can spend caps and scheduled tasks be set per client, so one client's article budget never bleeds into another's? And on WordPress, do articles land as drafts by default? I'd want a human pass on tone before anything goes live under a client's name.

beacon.sh: Open-source self-improving memory for AI coding agents Beacon turns agent sessions across Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, and 20+ other harnesses into a compounding knowledge layer, so every agent starts smarter than the last. It captures every agent trace across your environment and turns activity into clear operational visibility. Get started for free at beacon.sh

One of my favorite things about Beacon is that it makes your coding agents smarter the more you use them.

For everyone in the Product Hunt community building and shipping with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or other coding agents, you've probably experienced how frustrating it is to solve the same problem multiple times across different sessions and tools!

<

Memory is where most agents fall apart for me, so this is the right problem to go after. The part id push on is source and staleness. A memory learned from a trace 3 weeks ago can be confidently wrong after a refactor, and then every agent sharing it inherits the mistake. Does each memory point back to the trace it came from, and does anything expire it when the code it refers to changes? We ma

Love the idea of carrying lessons across coding agents. How does Beacon handle it when two agents learn conflicting things about the same codebase?

producthunt.body:
Alsona: AI agents that turn buying signals into booked sales calls 95% of prospects aren't ready to buy when you reach out. Alsona finds the ones showing buying intent right now. It tracks 32+ signals across hiring, funding, tech changes, reviews, ad spend, and more, then scores companies against your ICP and explains why they're worth contacting. AI agents turn those signals into personalized LinkedIn and email outreach, helping you start conversations while the buying window is open. Alsona helps you book calls directly with the 5% who is ready to buy today.

Hey Product Hunt,

I’m Jaclyn, co-founder and CEO of Alsona.

Alsona finds the companies that are in market right now, so you can reach them before your competitors even know they’re looking.

We built it for people who do their own outbound and secretly hate it. If your current strategy is buying a list and hoping somebody on it needs you this week, hi, this is for y

Loking forward to try Alsona soon - one question, does it also recommend changes on the web to better target the acutla ICP? it scans for ICP but wondering if there is a way to find the signals (what was scanned) if you detect the ICP doesn't match with the during the onboarding to your real ICP (e.g. copy on web is not updated)

Im very happy with these company

producthunt.author: fmerian
producthunt.body:
Plurai Simulation: A simulated world that makes your agent improve on every run Find your agent’s worst bugs before your users do. One command in Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot builds a digital twin of your agent’s world: synthetic personas and documents, plus mocked tools, APIs and databases, in sandboxes that never touch production.

Hey Product Hunt, Ilan from Plurai here.

Before Plurai, I built simulation for autonomous driving. Self-driving cars earned trust in millions of simulated miles before real roads. AI agents still skip that step.

Most agent testing puts a fake user in front of your agent and grades the chat. The transcript says "refund issued." Did the refund actually happen?

Building a digital twin of an AI agent's tools, APIs, and databases for realistic testing is a powerful idea. Can Plurai automatically replay production failures against updated agent versions and verify that the fix works without introducing new regressions?

digital twin of the whole stack for agent testing is clever 🔥 how long does a full sim run take?

Scalekit: MCP gateway for production agents that acts on your behalf Let your agents use 30,000+ tools across 600+ apps, from Salesforce to GitHub, through one MCP gateway. AgentKit handles auth and integrations, so every action runs as the user who asked, within the scopes they granted. Give each agent only the tools its job needs with Virtual MCP Servers. Add internal APIs as custom connectors. Use Triggers to start an agent the moment an email lands. Built for developers taking agents to production: every call is logged. Free tier: 10,000 tool calls a month.

producthunt.author: zaczuo
producthunt.body:
Creatify Max: Your ad teammate, from strategy to creation to launch Max is your teammate for paid ads. Share a product URL or brief and Max makes video ads, sets up campaigns on Meta and TikTok, and watches results 24/7, flagging what to fix next. You make the calls: nothing goes live without your approval.

Hello, Product Hunters! 👋

I’m Yinan, CEO of Creatify. Some of you may remember us from our URL to video ads launch. Thanks to this community, we became the #1 Product of the Day.

Today, we’re launching the biggest product we’ve built so far: Creatify Max. Creating an ad is only one part of the job. Paid media teams still spend hours checking dashboards

Creatify Max looks like a great step forward in AI-powered advertising! The human approval layer is a thoughtful addition, keeping automation practical while ensuring control. Congratulations to the team on the launch! 👏

The promise sounds good, but paid media gets messy at the edges. Tracking issues, rejected ads, weird attribution. I would love to see those cases in a demo.

producthunt.author: justin2025
producthunt.body:
Glasshand: Give your agent a real iPhone and Mac Glasshand gives your AI agents real iPhones and Macs to work on. Connect Claude Code, Codex, or any other agent, and it can rent a device with a single prompt. The hardware sits in our data center, and your agent uses it the way you would: posting on TikTok, booking an Uber, or building and testing iOS apps. Each device is yours alone for as long as you rent it. When you’re done, we erase your data and factory-reset it.

Hey everyone. I’m Trevor, creator of Glasshand.

We’re the team behind Solid, from MIT, Berkeley, and Waterloo. We’ve raised $6M to build toward one goal: agents with human-level autonomy.


Agents are already smart enough for most of what you’d ask them to do, but a simple task on a phone can still leave yours waiting for you to open an app and tap a few buttons.

So Congrats on the launch! I wonder if this could replace our hardware to test a macOS agent we deploy through Intune. A few questions: - Do we get admin rights, with sudo to install LaunchDaemons? - Can we enrol the Mac in our own MDM (Intune through Company Portal) and install custom configuration profiles? - Which macOS version is it on, and how stable is the public IP and gateway? This is a great idea. I’ve found it annoying when building to have to manually test holding, scrubbing, finger-related UI interactions for my app… would be awesome to have my agents be able to interact with my product like I or anyone else would, without having to push and deploy everything for a little update to see if my scrubbing mechanic is a little better. Great work 👌🔥

producthunt.author: zaczuo
producthunt.body:
S.Space: Your team and everyone's AI agents, in one workspace Everyone on your team has an AI agent, and none of them work together, so you copy, paste and re-explain all day. S.Space is one workspace for your team and everyone's agents. Bring the ones you already use, like Claude Code and Codex, from any vendor. Agents reach out, hand work to each other and bring you finished results, with shared memory so you explain things once. Agents act, you approve what matters. Free to start. Built by the team behind AutoGen.

How are you planning to document the hand-off and shared-memory model? If a team already runs Claude Code or Codex, I'd want to know what context S.Space passes between agents and what each one can see before I plug them in.

Congratulations on the launch! This is really cool. Bringing everything together in one place makes perfect sense.

Congrats to the whole team 🫰

Putting the work in shared pages and databases instead of in chat is the right call. Chat scrolls away, a page doesn't.

producthunt.body:
Wanaka Studio: Make and publish 3D games with the first AI game engine The first all-in-one, AI-native game engine. An AI agent builds your AAA-style 3D game. You can edit it directly in a synced visual editor. No code. Auto-rigging, multiplayer, and 1-click publish built in. Uses ~80% fewer tokens and generates faster than Claude Opus 5.5 + Unity.

Hey Product Hunt! 👋


 I'm Yang, Founder & CEO of Wanaka.

Hey Product Hunt, Ilan from Plurai here.

Before Plurai, I built simulation for autonomous driving. Self-driving cars earned trust in millions of simulated miles before real roads. AI agents still skip that step.

Most agent testing puts a fake user in front of your agent and grades the chat. The transcript says "refund issued." Did the refund actually happen?

Building a digital twin of an AI agent's tools, APIs, and databases for realistic testing is a powerful idea. Can Plurai automatically replay production failures against updated agent versions and verify that the fix works without introducing new regressions?

digital twin of the whole stack for agent testing is clever 🔥 how long does a full sim run take?

source_items.author: justin2025
source_items.body:
Glasshand: Give your agent a real iPhone and Mac Glasshand gives your AI agents real iPhones and Macs to work on. Connect Claude Code, Codex, or any other agent, and it can rent a device with a single prompt. The hardware sits in our data center, and your agent uses it the way you would: posting on TikTok, booking an Uber, or building and testing iOS apps. Each device is yours alone for as long as you rent it. When you’re done, we erase your data and factory-reset it.

Hey everyone. I’m Trevor, creator of Glasshand.

We’re the team behind Solid, from MIT, Berkeley, and Waterloo. We’ve raised $6M to build toward one goal: agents with human-level autonomy.


Agents are already smart enough for most of what you’d ask them to do, but a simple task on a phone can still leave yours waiting for you to open an app and tap a few buttons.

So Congrats on the launch! I wonder if this could replace our hardware to test a macOS agent we deploy through Intune. A few questions: - Do we get admin rights, with sudo to install LaunchDaemons? - Can we enrol the Mac in our own MDM (Intune through Company Portal) and install custom configuration profiles? - Which macOS version is it on, and how stable is the public IP and gateway? This is a great idea. I’ve found it annoying when building to have to manually test holding, scrubbing, finger-related UI interactions for my app… would be awesome to have my agents be able to interact with my product like I or anyone else would, without having to push and deploy everything for a little update to see if my scrubbing mechanic is a little better. Great work 👌🔥
